alignments.note: Participle with supplied subordinator when (rule 86), discontinuous under rule 15.
Substantival article before a participle supplies the pronominal word and nothing else (rules 22 and 32).
Participle rendered as a finite passive; the copula is its helper.
No English determiner for the article to anchor (rule 23).
Demonstrative, made the English subject of the ASV's recast; it stands alone and determines nothing.

The article takes the supplied indefinite a. Rule 38 does not empty it here: in the ASV's recast houtos stands alone as the subject this and does not occupy the determiner slot of the article's own noun, so no other source word competes for that slot, and rules 51 and 92 give the supplied determiner to the article, headed on it. Rule 92 forbids in terms handing a supplied determiner to a noun standing behind its own article. Reading the article unrepresented under rule 38 and a man whole on anthrōpōi is the competing analysis and was the accepted one.
Predicate adjective made attributive in the ASV's recast.
Head noun recast as the predicate nominal; the determiner stands with its own article under rule 92.

review_notes: Corrected the article ho from unrepresented to aligned on the supplied a: rule 38 empties an article only where the demonstrative occupies the English determiner slot, and in this recast this is the standalone subject while a determines the article's own noun.
The demonstrative keeps a bare this and the copula stays on the expressed ēn.
